context.prd-excerpt:
Feature: Save a link (slug: save-link, must-have).
As someone collecting links, I want to store a URL with an optional title, so that I can come back to it without keeping a browser tab open.
A POST endpoint that accepts a URL and an optional title, stores it, and returns the stored record including its generated id and creation timestamp.
The URL is the only required field. If no title is supplied the field is stored as null rather than being derived from the page, because fetching the page would make the endpoint depend on the network.
Considerations (verbatim from the feature): Duplicate URLs are allowed. Deduplication sounds obviously desirable but needs a rule for what to do with the existing record's tags and timestamp, and that decision is not worth making for a fixture.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS TASK: `url` carries NO unique constraint and NO unique index. Two rows with the same url are a supported state, not a bug. Do not add uniqueness to url.

task.objective:
Declare the `Link` SQLAlchemy model - the table that stores one saved URL with an optional title and the time it was stored - exactly as the save-link feature's data model specifies it, and register it on `app/models/__init__.py` so `Base.metadata` knows about the table.
This task builds the storage that the Layer 2 endpoints satisfy their acceptance criteria through. It satisfies none of save-link's criteria itself: those are HTTP-level (201, 422) and are met by L2-001 (POST /links), which writes into this table. Correspondingly, this task defines no route, no Pydantic schema and no validation - a bad URL is rejected by L2-001's request schema, not by the column.

requirements.requirement:
Create `app/models/link.py` with exactly this content:
"""The Link model: one stored URL with an optional title."""
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from sqlalchemy import DateTime, Integer, Text from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from app.database import Base
def utcnow() -> datetime: """Return the current UTC time as a naive datetime, to microsecond resolution.""" return datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)
class Link(Base): """A saved link: a URL, an optional title, and when it was stored."""
__tablename__ = "links"
id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True) url: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=False) title: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True) created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column( DateTime, nullable=False, default=utcnow )
Decisions embedded above that must be preserved exactly as written:
- `__tablename__ = "links"`. Lower-case plural. L1-003 writes a foreign key targeting `"links.id"` by that exact string, so renaming the table breaks a task that cannot see this file.
- `url` has NO `unique=True` and NO unique index. The save-link feature states verbatim that duplicate URLs are allowed and deduplication is deliberately not done. A unique constraint here would make a supported state raise IntegrityError.
- `title` is `Mapped[str | None]` with `nullable=True`. An untitled link stores SQL NULL. Do not substitute an empty string, and do not add a default.
- `created_at` uses `default=utcnow` - a PYTHON-side default evaluated at INSERT - and NOT `server_default=func.now()`. SQLite's `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` has one-second resolution, so two links saved in the same second would carry identical timestamps and the newest-first ordering that L2-002 must guarantee would be a coin flip. `utcnow` returns microsecond resolution, which makes that ordering deterministic.
- `utcnow` returns a NAIVE datetime (`.replace(tzinfo=None)`) holding UTC. SQLAlchemy's SQLite DATETIME type stores a string with no offset and reads back a naive datetime, so writing an aware value and reading a naive one would make `written == read` false. Naive-in, naive-out keeps the round trip equal. Do not use `datetime.utcnow()`: it is deprecated from Python 3.12 and this file must not emit a DeprecationWarning.
- `utcnow` is passed as the function itself (`default=utcnow`), not called (`default=utcnow()`). Calling it would freeze one timestamp at import time and give every row the same `created_at`.
- Do NOT define a `tags` relationship, do NOT import `Tag`, and do NOT reference `link_tags`. `app/models/tag.py` and `app/models/link_tag.py` do not exist in this worktree. L1-003 adds the relationship to this file later.
- Do NOT call `Base.metadata.create_all` anywhere in this file.

Replace the content of `app/models/__init__.py` with exactly this:
"""SQLAlchemy models for Link Shelf."""
from app.models.link import Link
__all__ = ["Link"]
This import is what registers the `links` table on `Base.metadata`. `tests/conftest.py` runs `import app.models` before calling `Base.metadata.create_all`, so a model that is not imported here has no table and every test touching it fails with "no such table: links".
Add ONLY the `Link` import. Do not add `Tag` or `LinkTag`: their modules do not exist in this worktree, and importing them raises ModuleNotFoundError at collection time. L1-002 adds `Tag` to this same file from its own worktree and L1-003 adds `LinkTag`; the final file names all three.

Do NOT create or edit any other file. Specifically: do not touch `app/database.py`, `app/main.py`, `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/test_setup.py`, `pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt` or `.gitignore`. Do not create a Pydantic schema, a router, a route or a migration - this project has no migration tool, the schema is created from `Base.metadata`. Do not run `git init` and do not touch `.git`.

exports.interface:
# app/models/link.py from datetime import datetime
from sqlalchemy import DateTime, Integer, Text from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from app.database import Base
def utcnow() -> datetime: """Return the current UTC time as a naive datetime, to microsecond resolution.""" ...
class Link(Base): __tablename__ = "links"
id: Mapped[int] # integer primary key, autoincrement url: Mapped[str] # Text, NOT NULL, NOT unique title: Mapped[str | None] # Text, nullable created_at: Mapped[datetime] # DateTime, NOT NULL, default=utcnow (naive UTC)
Import as: `from app.models import Link` (also available as `from app.models.link import Link`, and `from app.models.link import utcnow`)
Downstream contract: - Table name is `links`; the primary key column is `links.id`. L1-003's foreign key targets `"links.id"` by that string. - `url` is deliberately NOT unique. Saving the same URL twice creates two rows with different ids. Any endpoint that assumes one row per URL is wrong. - `title` is NULL when omitted. L2-002 must report it as JSON `null`, never drop the key. - `created_at` is assigned by Python at INSERT with microsecond resolution and is a NAIVE datetime holding UTC. Ordering newest-first is `select(Link).order_by(Link.created_at.desc())`; two links inserted back to back get distinct timestamps, so that ordering is stable. - No relationship attribute exists yet. L1-003 adds `Link.tags`.

# app/models/__init__.py after this task """SQLAlchemy models for Link Shelf."""
from app.models.link import Link
__all__ = ["Link"]
Downstream contract: `import app.models` registers the `links` table on `Base.metadata`, which is what makes `Base.metadata.create_all` in `tests/conftest.py` create it. L1-002 adds `Tag` and L1-003 adds `LinkTag` to this same file; a later task must ADD to the import list, never replace it.
